answer_sentences.text: Yes — the 2023 circular is the current rule to cite for penal charges in your loan policy.
answer_sentences.quote: On a review of the practices followed by REs for charging penal interest/charges on loans, the following instructions are issued for adoption.

answer_sentences.text: It specifically says REs must have a Board-approved policy on penal charges or similar charges on loans.
answer_sentences.quote: The REs shall formulate a Board approved policy on penal charges or similar charges on loans, by whatever name called.

answer_sentences.text: It also says REs should not add any extra component to the interest rate and must follow the guidelines in letter and spirit.
answer_sentences.quote: The REs shall not introduce any additional component to the rate of interest and ensure compliance to these guidelines in both letter and spirit.

answer_sentences.text: The circular further states that penal charges should be fair, transparent, and disclosed in the loan agreement and KFS, and not levied as penal interest added to the rate of interest.
answer_sentences.quote: Penalty, if charged, for non-compliance of material graph terms and conditions of loan contract by the borrower shall be treated as ‘penal charges’ and shall not be levied in the form of ‘penal interest’ that is added to the rate of interest charged on the advances. ... The REs shall formulate a Board approved policy on penal charges or similar charges on loans, by whatever name called. ... The quantum and reason for penal charges shall be clearly disclosed by REs to the customers in the loan agreement and most important terms & conditions / Key Fact Statement (KFS) as applicable
